note: Started 2026-08-16, first substantive verdict recorded 2026-08-19. Still a worklist: one of ten entries has had its source opened. The session that opened this file had no outbound network beyond server-side search, so every claim_support verdict was left 'unchecked'; egress from the host this was continued on reaches aclanthology.org, doi.org, asd-ste100.org and en.wikipedia.org, while aslopubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com, direct.mit.edu and chronicle.com refuse automated requests with 403. Bibliographic metadata alone remains insufficient for a claim_support verdict: a catalogue record establishes that a work exists, never what it argues.

entries.cited_as: Kuhn 2014 survey of controlled natural languages, Computational Linguistics 40(1)

citation_accuracy.note: Tobias Kuhn, "A Survey and Classification of Controlled Natural Languages", Computational Linguistics 40(1):121-170, 2014. Venue, volume and issue match; the corpus does not state a page range, so none was checkable.

claim_support.quote: For type C, two studies on AECMA-SE showed that the use of controlled English significantly improves text comprehension, with a particularly large effect for complex texts and non-native speakers (Shubert et al. 1995; Chervak, Drury, and Ouellette 1996). The results of other studies were similar but not significant (Stewart 1998).
claim_support.note: Opened at aclanthology.org/J14-1005.pdf (sha256 befc7ebb73c5bfb9de26f66b7a836465de7e6ae8de0fd4e527051165dbd44855); the quoted passage is section 5.5 'Evaluations', page 145. Two things follow, and they point opposite ways to what this entry previously supposed. First, the doubt recorded here on 2026-08-16 - whether a classification survey summarises comprehension outcomes at all - is settled: it does, and the three works it names are aircraft-documentation studies (Shubert et al. 1995, Journal of Technical Writing and Communication 25(4):347-369; Chervak, Drury and Ouellette 1996, Proceedings of the Tenth Meeting on Human Factors Issues in Aircraft Maintenance and Inspection, 123-136; Stewart 1998, master's thesis, University of British Columbia, on comprehension of aircraft maintenance procedures by non-native English speakers). Second, that makes this source cut against c-032 rather than support it: c-032 states that no empirical outcome studies were found in open sources, and this survey - already on the investigation's own source list - names three. What the survey does not establish is whether any of them meets c-032's stated bar of an RCT or strong quasi-experiment; Chervak is described as a field evaluation, and settling that requires opening the three studies themselves, which this audit has not done. Recorded as 'contradicts' on the existence question with that limit stated, rather than 'partially-supports', which would read as the claim surviving narrowed. Separately: the earlier note said the analysis attributes this summary to the survey. It does not - 'kuhn' appears nowhere in analysis.md, and the investigation's prose asserts the absence of such studies rather than their presence. See 05-analysis/corrections.md.

entries.cited_as: STEMG's own training material — "STE is not a simplified version of English for the writers, only for the readers"

citation_accuracy.note: A STEMG training document at this URL exists and is indexed. The host is unreachable from the auditing environment, so neither the document's date nor its issue could be established.

claim_support.note: Search results carry the same proposition in different words: the objective is simplified text for readers, and separately STE is not a simplified version of English for the writers. The corpus states that in one sentence. Under the same-meaning test that is equivalent wording, not a discrepancy, so the expected verdict is 'supports' with wording 'equivalent' once the primary document can be opened. Still unchecked only because no source could be read from the auditing environment. One thing to fix in the prose independently: the investigation prints this inside quotation marks, which asserts exact words, and it appears to compress two sentences into one.

entries.rights: ASD-STE100 material is distributed free of charge but is not open-licensed (see c-009). Confirm quoting permissions before reproducing more than short extracts.

entries.cited_as: Kincaid et al., 1975, readability formulas developed for the US Navy

claim_support.note: The load-bearing part is purpose, not existence: the claim is that the formulas were built to estimate difficulty of existing text for procurement, not to guide writing. That is the hinge of the Goodhart argument the whole series carries forward.
Supports the claim that STE removes devices persuasion depends on. Effect direction and size both matter here and neither is stated in the corpus.
